newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe unions, minister clash over Mugabe trip.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe unions, minister clash over Mugabe trip.

text.p: Zimbabwe's Congress of Trade Unions (ZCTU) and a senior cabinet minister have clashed over President Robert Mugabe's trip to the World Food Summit in Rome during a crippling strike by local nurses and doctors.

ZCTU secretary-general Morgan Tsvangirayi told Zimbabwe state television on Monday night that Mugabe -- who has in the past ignored accusations that he prefers to travel the world at the expense of his domestic duties -- should not have gone to Rome late on Monday, leaving the strike unresolved.
"This is a critical issue requiring his attention," he said.

But acting Public Service, Labour and Social Welfare Minister Ntahan Shamuyarira defended the trip, saying Mugabe's presence at the summit was crucial because Zimbabwe is an agriculture-based country.

"He has to be there...and it's not for some irresponsible trade union leader to tell him how he uses his time," he told Tsvangirayi, whose federation has called for a two-day nationwide strike starting on Tuesday aimed at pressing the government to resolve a three-week strike by nurses and doctors.
The government has vowed not to bow to pressure.
